value.rationale: Variable exponent d is a native defining parameter of this fixed-point-free family, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The theorem quantifies the onset and width of bistability (two attracting two-cycles separated by a repelling one) and shows it is inevitable at high exponent for any fixed strictly alternating parameters. Its exact exponential cycle-location asymptotics explain loss of branch-scale numerical resolution and give a structural completion of the originating numerical bifurcation study. These are not consequences of the known quadratic cusp alone.
